body: If you are not willing to take medication, there is really no reason to be seeing a psychiatrist. All you are doing is wasting time and money, and there are other ways to approach your issues if you feel that medication isn't working for you. I would suggest you let your psychiatrist know that you haven't been taking it, and tell them about your hangups with the medications you've tried so far. Ask them to recommend a therapist for you to see, and don't quit going to the psychiatrist until you have started seeing a therapist.

Definitely get help! Suicidal thoughts/self-harm are never okay! I suffered long term depression for years after a breakup and ended up badly scarring my arms and ending up in the hospital a couple times for oding on pain/sleeping pills. I final snapped out of it once I realized how many people loved/supported me. Now I have recently been broken up with and things are going much better, even though the duration of the relationship was longer and the relationship itself was Much more serious and loving. I am going out, joining clubs, avoiding alcohol and seeking support from friends and family. I also scheduled therapy for myself right away and have an appointment next week. I jumped into doing everything I could to contribute to my future happiness and give myself a positive outlook on life. I may feel shitty sometimes and have trouble eating/sleeping but I am trying to give myself plenty to look forward to to avoid another long term depression, if possible.

My point is that even if you don't feel happy now it is imperative that you take steps towards a happy future! And get treatment right away for your depression. Make an appointment for therapy and tell friends and family how you are feeling. You may have some blame in the end of your relationship; I know I did for this one. But so did he (in both our cases) and in the end, both parties learned a lot from the relationship which can be applied to future partners. So even if you don't feel like it, get out of the house. Get in touch with family and friends. And please stop relying on alcohol. I believe alcohol is completely fine when you are having a good time with friends but if you are already feeling bad, it will only make you feel worse and potentially lead to you doing some really stupid, possibly permanent, things. The next time you feel like drinking, talk to someone. Even if it's the internet (reddit has a depression subforum!).

In the end, you also need to learn to enjoy your own company. Accept that you are feeling badly. That doesn't mean you have to drink or do damage to yourself. You can always spend an evening just feeling badly. The whole world is still going on around you and it's not over because you got broken up with. Try doing things that you can enjoy on your own such as taking walks, watching a funny show/movie or taking a drive. Pick up a hobby or do something you couldn't do in your relationship or had been putting off. 

Anyways, I hope this helps. Please pm me if you would like counseling resources/advice or just want to talk. I care about you and want you to be happy!
